module_title: Types of Poverty and Early Estimation Committees
introduction: At this beginner level, we will understand how poverty is defined globally versus in India, and look at the early committees that established the foundation of the 'Poverty Line' based on nutritional intake.

core_concepts.title: Relative vs. Absolute Poverty
core_concepts.description:
1. Relative Poverty: Measures 'inequality' of income (e.g., A middle-class person is relatively poor compared to a billionaire). It is measured in developed nations. 
2. Absolute Poverty: When a person cannot afford even the most basic survival needs (food, clothing, shelter). Developing nations like India measure 'Absolute Poverty' by drawing a fixed 'Poverty Line'.

core_concepts.title: Y. K. Alagh Committee (1979)
core_concepts.description:
The first committee to define the poverty line in India scientifically. Its core basis was entirely 'Calorie Consumption'. 
Recommendation: Anyone consuming less than '2400 kcal per day' in rural areas and '2100 kcal per day' in urban areas was classified as poor. (Rural areas require more calories due to heavy physical labor).

core_concepts.title: Lakdawala Committee (1993)
core_concepts.description: This committee retained the Alagh Committee's calorie criteria but made a major change. It stated that inflation is different in every state, so a single national poverty line is inaccurate. It recommended calculating 'State-specific poverty lines'.

core_concepts.title: Basic Definition of Unemployment
core_concepts.description: Unemployment does NOT mean everyone who is not working is unemployed (e.g., students or retired elders are not counted). An 'unemployed' person is someone who is in the labor force, is 'willing and able' to work, is 'actively seeking' work, but is 'unable to find' a job.

important_entities.name: NSSO (National Sample Survey Office)
important_entities.significance: Official data regarding poverty and employment in India is collected through massive nationwide 'Consumption Expenditure Surveys' conducted by the NSSO (now part of NSO). The Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) used this data to estimate the poverty ratio.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common exam trap: The Poverty Line in India is NEVER determined based on a person's 'Income'. It is strictly measured based on 'Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure' (MPCE) — meaning it is calculated based on how much money people are spending to survive, not earning.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 24 in the Village, 21 in the City
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Rural = 2400 kcal (Physical work). Urban = 2100 kcal (Mental/Sedentary work).

exam_strategy_tips: The chronology of the poverty committees is repeatedly asked. Memorize the order: Alagh (1979) -> Lakdawala (1993) -> Tendulkar (2009) -> Rangarajan (2014).
